title: Froggy Moore Blues credit dispute with Melrose and Hafer
summary: Carew objects to a record crediting Seitz, Oliver and Melrose on Morton's tune, blaming Melrose and a Hafer note, and the license he gave Melrose.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yes, well I have a recording that he made of Froggy Moore, and they called it Froggy Moore Blues. I don't know, I'm not sweating about that yet. They called it Froggy Moore Blues, and on the outside of the cover, it says this tune, the King Oliver tune, Froggy Moore's blues, so and so and so, went on like that. All King Oliver ever did was to record Froggy Moore Blues once.

Sure it is, entirely. But on the inside, worse yet, on the record, he says, he gave the name and then he said, Seitz, John Seitz, the other Seitz, King Oliver, Melrose, he named about four people and then Morton.
Frank Melrose? Well, no, I think it was Walter Melrose.

Walter Melrose. No, I think it was Walter, yeah, Walter Melrose. The publisher. He never wrote anything. No, four people had their names there. And on that instrumental thing, while Jelly Roll was the only one, he wrote it five years before Seitz brothers ever saw it. Spikes, Spikes, Spikes. Yeah, Spikes. Spikes, Spikes. Yeah, Spikes. Spikes.
Yeah, and that was the work of George Hafer. He's the guy that wrote that thing up.
I don't know why Hafer got mixed up on that.
He generally was very active. He wasn't mixed up. He was mixed up by Melrose. That's who mixed him up. Yeah, exactly. Melrose, you see, I...
Dan Melrose always wants to claim everything.

I was crazy enough to give Melrose a non-exclusive license to publish the thing, see. And to get so much on published music he published and on recordings or on performances. And split that on certain. I thought he would push it, but he never had, see. He just sits still when it comes up while Hafer does it. He did. Hafer wrote in the Melrose book, you know, Piano Solos. He put a cockeyed explanation up above there about Sweetheart of Mind, which uses Fraga on more blues as a chorus. Well, I got after him on that and I choked him off. I got him on that, cut it out, change it, and they had to stop publishing it in England as such. Yeah. But every chance he gets, he pulls one. So as I say, I'm going to write... Who put that out again now? I forget who put that out right away. Verve, is it Verve? Yeah, Verve. Verve did, yeah.
That's right. I've got that right. I'm going to write...
Misery and the Blues, is that it? No, it's Fraga and the More blues. Yeah, but that's on... Oh, Misery and the Blues, yeah. That's the name of the album. That's the name of the album.
